ActivePointsOf.text: The connection points of an object, i.e. TinyCAD's GetActive: the visible pins of a placed symbol, a power symbol's point, the point of an input/output label, or both ends of a bus slash. Wires, junctions and shapes have none. Wire snapping and junction checks use these.
ActivePointsOf.returns: array of points; empty when the object has no connection points

PointNotEqual.text: True when two points differ by more than the 0.001 tolerance TinyCAD uses when comparing points (the opposite of PointsClose).
PointNotEqual.returns: True if the points are different

TWireEngine.Create.text: Creates the engine for editing one sheet of a design. It keeps the lists the merge and junction passes use (discarded wires, dragged wires, the junction to-do list).

params.ADesign: the design (used to give new objects ids)

TWireEngine.Destroy.text: Frees the working lists. The sheet and its objects are not owned by the engine.

TWireEngine.Opts.text: The options of the sheet being edited (snap grid, auto-junction and auto-snap settings, zoom).

TWireEngine.IndexInDrawing.text: Finds an object in the sheet's drawing list; used to forget wires that a merge or discard has already removed.
TWireEngine.IndexInDrawing.returns: position in the list, or -1 when the object is not on the sheet

TWireEngine.DeleteObject.text: Removes an object from the sheet (the list frees it) and clears the single-selection reference if it pointed at that object.

TWireEngine.AddObject.text: Adds an object to the sheet, giving it a new object id first if it has none.

params.Obj: the object to add; the sheet takes ownership

TWireEngine.AddNewJunction.text: Creates a junction dot at Q and adds it to the sheet (TinyCAD's AddNewJunction). It does not check whether one is already there, as in TinyCAD.

TWireEngine.StickyPoint.text: Where the cursor "sticks" while drawing (a port of GetStickyPoint): a pin or other connection point, or the nearest point on a wire, when within the snap range; otherwise the grid point. Also reports whether sticking here would join three or more things so a junction is wanted. With auto-snap off it returns the grid point.

params.Pins: consider connection points of symbols, power symbols and labels
params.IsStuck: set True when the result is a pin or wire point
params.IsJunction: set True when a junction would be needed there

TWireEngine.TodoAdd.text: Appends a point or a line to the list of places whose junction requirement must be re-checked.

params.A: the point, or the line's start
params.B: the line's end (ignored for a point)

TWireEngine.AddObjectToTodo.text: Notes what needs a junction check because of this object: a wire's whole line, a junction's point, or an object's connection points. Does nothing when auto-junction is off.

params.Obj: the object that was added, moved or removed

TWireEngine.CheckJunctionRequirement#3.text: Checks every point along the line A-B where something touches it (wire ends, junctions, connection points) and applies the single-point check at each, in the order TinyCAD does (sorted points, no duplicates).

params.PerformSplit: allow wires to be split and merged, not just junctions added or removed

TWireEngine.CheckJunctionRequirement#2.text: Decides whether a junction belongs at Q: adds one when three or more things meet at a wire end, removes one that is no longer needed (merging the two collinear wires it joined), and with PerformSplit splits a wire that another wire ends in the middle of. A port of TinyCAD's CJunctionUtils.

params.PerformSplit: allow wires to be split and merged

TWireEngine.CheckTodoList.text: Runs the junction check for everything on the to-do list, empties the list, and (when splitting) deletes the wires the checks marked as merged away.

TWireEngine.EndDrag.text: Finishes an edit of the wires in the dragged list (CDragUtils::End): drops wires that are gone, merges them with collinear neighbours, cleans zero-length ones, then runs the junction checks.

TWireEngine.MergeLinePoint.text: Entry point used after a wire has been stored: treats it as the dragged wire and runs the merge, clean and junction pass so it joins neighbouring wires and gets junctions and splits.

params.Obj: the wire just added to the sheet

TWireTool.Create.text: Creates a wire or line tool bound to an engine and sets it up as TinyCAD does: wires use the 90 degree angle mode and the default wire style; plain lines draw at any angle.

params.AEngine: the engine for the sheet being drawn on
params.AKind: xWire for wires, xLineEx2 for lines

TWireTool.BeginEdit.text: Resets the tool to "waiting for the first point": no segment in progress, no sticking, no segments stored yet.

TWireTool.StickyFor.text: The point to use for a mouse position: wires stick to pins and wires through the engine; plain lines just snap to the grid.

TWireTool.ToAngle.text: Applies the angle rule to the end point B of the segment being drawn: in 90 degree mode it picks horizontal-first or vertical-first for the dog-leg; in 45 degree mode it forces B onto the nearest 45 degree line; otherwise it does nothing.

TWireTool.LButtonDown.text: Handles a left click as TinyCAD's line tool does. The first click starts a segment (adding a junction if it starts on a wire or pin junction and copying the style of a wire under it). Later clicks store the segment (as an L of two wires in 90 degree mode when the end sticks) and carry on from the end, or finish when the end stuck to a pin or wire.

TWireTool.RButtonDown.text: Ends the wire being drawn (right click or finish): removes junctions that are no longer needed at its ends and goes back to waiting for a first point.
TWireTool.RButtonDown.returns: True when a segment was in progress

TWireTool.DblLButtonDown.text: A double click: places the last segment and ends the wire.

TWireTool.LButtonUp.text: On releasing the mouse: if the user pressed and dragged a real distance (more than 10 units) the wire is placed and ended, so press-drag-release draws a wire; otherwise the tool stays in click-click mode.

TWireTool.Move.text: Follows the mouse: while a segment is being drawn it updates the end point (with sticking) and applies the angle rule; while waiting for the first point it just tracks where a click would land.

TWireTool.EndEdit.text: Called when the tool is dropped: finishes any wire in progress.

TWireTool.Preview.text: Gives the middle point of the rubber band to draw: the corner of the dog-leg in 90 degree mode, or the start point when the band is one straight piece.

params.Corner: set to the corner point of the rubber band

ReferencePoint.text: Where an object "is" for finding its ladder line: the middle of a placed symbol's connection points, otherwise the middle of its box, otherwise its first point (junctions use their point).
ReferencePoint.returns: the reference point in design units

LineNumberOfObject.text: Finds the ladder line an object sits on: the first ladder on the sheet whose rails enclose the object's reference point, and the line number at that height.
LineNumberOfObject.returns: True when the object is between a ladder's rails

params.Number: set to the line number (0 when not on a ladder)

Where.text: Formats a line reference for display: the plain line number on the same sheet, "sheet.line" on another sheet, or "?" when the object is not on a ladder.

params.OwnSheet: 1-based number of the sheet the text is on
params.R: the sheet number and line to show

TextFor.text: Works out what a linked text should say. Mode 0 gives the ladder line of its target; mode 1 gives the lines of the other symbols that share the target's reference, sorted by sheet then line and separated by commas ("-" when there are none, "?" when the target no longer exists).
TextFor.returns: the resolved text without prefix or suffix

params.OwnSheet: zero-based index of the sheet the text is on

UpdateLinks.text: Recomputes the text of every linked text object in the design and refreshes its layout. Call after anything that can change a line number: moving, adding or deleting objects, or editing a ladder.

TUndoManager.Create.text: Creates an undo manager for a design with a depth limit of 100 steps and empty history.

params.ADesign: the design whose history is kept

TUndoManager.SetDesign.text: Points the manager at a different design (or none), allows empty sheets on it, and clears the history.

TUndoManager.Reset.text: Clears the undo and redo history and any change in progress.

TUndoManager.BeginChange.text: First half of a change that might turn out to do nothing: takes the snapshot now but does not put it on the undo stack yet.

params.ACaption: name of the action, shown for Undo
params.ASel: ids of the selected objects before the change
params.ASheet: the sheet being shown before the change

TUndoManager.HasPending.text: Says whether BeginChange has been called without a matching Commit or Discard.
TUndoManager.HasPending.returns: True while a snapshot is waiting

TUndoManager.DiscardChange.text: Throws away the pending snapshot because nothing changed, so no undo step is created.

TUndoManager.CommitChange.text: Keeps the pending snapshot as an undo step (dropping the oldest when over the limit) and clears the redo history, since a new change has been made.

TUndoManager.Take.text: Captures the whole design as the text a save would write, together with the selection and sheet to restore.

TUndoManager.Restore.text: Reloads the design in place from a snapshot. Object ids only ever go up across a restore, so ids of deleted objects are not reused; the file name is kept.

params.ASel: set to the ids to select afterwards
params.ASheet: set to the sheet to show afterwards

TUndoManager.Push.text: Takes a snapshot immediately and puts it on the undo stack (the one-step form of BeginChange plus CommitChange). Call before making a change.

TUndoManager.CanUndo.text: Whether there is anything to undo.
TUndoManager.CanUndo.returns: True if the undo stack is not empty

TUndoManager.CanRedo.text: Whether there is anything to redo.
TUndoManager.CanRedo.returns: True if the redo stack is not empty

TUndoManager.UndoCount.text: How many steps can be undone.

TUndoManager.RedoCount.text: How many steps can be redone.

TUndoManager.UndoCaption.text: The name of the action Undo would reverse, for a menu or hint.
TUndoManager.UndoCaption.returns: the caption, or empty when nothing can be undone

TUndoManager.RedoCaption.text: The name of the action Redo would repeat, for a menu or hint.
TUndoManager.RedoCaption.returns: the caption, or empty when nothing can be redone

TUndoManager.Undo.text: Undoes the last step: saves the current state on the redo stack, then restores the previous snapshot. Gives back what to select and which sheet to show.
TUndoManager.Undo.returns: True if a step was undone

params.ASel: set to the ids to select after the undo
params.ASheet: set to the sheet to show after the undo

TUndoManager.Redo.text: Repeats the last undone step: saves the current state on the undo stack, then restores the redo snapshot.
TUndoManager.Redo.returns: True if a step was redone

params.ASel: set to the ids to select afterwards
params.ASheet: set to the sheet to show afterwards

PaperCount.text: Number of standard paper sizes in the table.

PaperInfo.text: One entry of the paper table: name, family and size in millimetres (landscape, width not less than height).

PaperIndexByName.text: Looks a paper up by its name, ignoring case.
PaperIndexByName.returns: its index, or -1 if there is no such paper

PaperDescription.text: A text for pick lists: name, size in millimetres and in inches.
PaperDescription.returns: for example "ANSI B (Tabloid) - 431.8 x 279.4 mm (17 x 11 in)"

PaperUnits.text: The page size in internal units (0.2 mm each) for a paper, rounding halves up so every size is rounded the same way.

params.Landscape: True for landscape, False for portrait

MatchPaper.text: Finds which standard paper a page size is, within a tolerance, in either orientation; when several fit the closest wins.
MatchPaper.returns: the paper's index, or -1 for a custom size

params.Tol: allowed difference per side, internal units
params.Landscape: set True if it matched in landscape

DescribePage.text: Describes a page size for display: the paper name and orientation, or "Custom W x H mm".

BorderRect.text: The border rectangle: the page inset by the same margin on every side (it stands for the printer's unprintable edge).

params.Margin: inset on each side, internal units

VariableNames.text: Lists the names of every title-block variable (SHEET, SHEETCOUNT, TITLE, REV ...) so a program can offer them in a pick list.

SheetOfText.text: The text "N of M" for a sheet: its number and the number of sheets in the file.

SheetsText.text: The sheet's Sheets field: "N of M" worked out automatically when auto-numbering is on, otherwise the text the user typed.

Lookup.text: Finds the value of one variable for a sheet (case already upper). Values come from the sheet's title block, revision history, paper, border and the file name.
Lookup.returns: True if the name is a known variable

ExpandVariables.text: Replaces every $(NAME) in Text with its value for the given sheet. "$$" gives a literal dollar sign; an unknown name or a "$(" with no closing bracket is left exactly as typed.
ExpandVariables.returns: the expanded text (unchanged if the sheet index is out of range)
